questions.q: Which pin marks the costodiaphragmatic recess?
questions.explain: The recess is pleural cavity beyond the lung margin, so it contains no lung tissue. Clinically it is the costophrenic angle.

questions.q: Which pin marks the lingula?
questions.explain: The lingula is a tongue-like part of the left lung that hugs the left side of the heart. The right lung has no lingula.

questions.q: Which pin marks the carina?
questions.explain: The carina is where the trachea bifurcates into the two main bronchi, at the level of the sternal angle (2nd rib).

questions.q: Which pin is the shorter, wider, more vertical main bronchus?
questions.explain: The right main bronchus is wider, shorter and more vertical than the left, so aspirated objects tend to end up on the right.

questions.q: Which pin is the vein that arches over the right main bronchus into the SVC?
questions.explain: The azygos vein ascends at the level of the carina and arches superiorly over the right main bronchus to drain into the SVC.

questions.q: Which pin is the pulmonary vessel that arches over the left main bronchus?
questions.explain: The left pulmonary artery crosses over (superior to) the left main bronchus, then runs posterior to the left superior lobar bronchus.

questions.q: Which pin marks the alveoli, the site of gas exchange?
questions.explain: Gas exchange occurs across the thin alveolar wall. Terminal bronchioles are conducting only; they have no alveoli.

questions.q: Which pin marks a primary muscle of inhalation?
questions.explain: The diaphragm and the external intercostals are the primary muscles of inhalation; the diaphragm is supplied by the phrenic nerve.

questions.q: Which pin marks the structure lying directly in front of the esophagus at the level of the lung roots?
questions.explain: The esophagus passes just posterior to the left atrium.

questions.q: Which pin marks the nerve that runs in front of the lung root and is motor to the diaphragm?
questions.explain: The phrenic nerve passes anterior to the root of the lung; the vagus nerve passes posterior to it.

questions.q: Which pleural layer lines the inner thoracic wall and the diaphragm?
questions.explain: Parietal pleura is the outside layer lining the pleural cavity. Visceral pleura covers the lung surface and enters the fissures.

questions.q: Which part of the parietal pleura extends above the clavicles?
questions.explain: The cervical pleura forms a cup-shaped dome over the lung apex, which is why lung tissue can be auscultated above the clavicles.

questions.q: A patient has a blunted costophrenic angle on chest X-ray. Fluid in which space is most likely?
questions.explain: Pleural effusion is fluid in the pleural cavity. Pulmonary edema is fluid in the alveoli.

questions.q: Which finding on chest X-ray points to pulmonary edema rather than pleural effusion?
options: Kerley B lines and cephalization of vessels
A pneumothorax line at the apex
A unilateral dense white lung base
questions.explain: Pulmonary edema is fluid in the alveoli: Kerley B lines, cephalization of vessels and an increased cardiothoracic ratio.

questions.q: Which feature belongs to the left lung only?
questions.explain: The left lung has two lobes, an oblique fissure only, a cardiac notch and a lingula, and two lobar bronchi.

questions.q: A toddler inhales a peanut. Which airway is it most likely to enter?
questions.explain: The right main bronchus is wider, shorter and more vertical, so inhaled foreign bodies pass into it more readily.

questions.q: How many lobar (secondary) bronchi arise from the right and left main bronchi?
questions.explain: One lobar bronchus per lobe: three on the right, two on the left. They give rise to segmental (tertiary) bronchi.

questions.q: Which structure is NOT part of the hilum (root) of the lung?
questions.explain: The hilum contains the pulmonary arteries and veins, the main bronchus, bronchial vessels, lymphatics and nerves. The esophagus lies in the mediastinum.

questions.q: The left main bronchus passes inferior to which structure and anterior to the esophagus?
questions.explain: The left main bronchus passes under the aortic arch and in front of the esophagus and thoracic aorta on its way to the left hilum.

questions.q: Oxygenated blood returns to the left atrium through how many pulmonary veins?
questions.explain: Four pulmonary veins, two from each lung, carry oxygen-rich blood to the left atrium. Pulmonary arteries carry oxygen-poor blood.

questions.q: Which cell secretes surfactant?
questions.explain: Type II pneumocytes secrete surfactant, which prevents alveolar collapse. Type I cells are the thin squamous gas-exchange cells.

questions.q: Which statement about bronchioles is correct?
options: They are the main site of gas exchange
They have cartilage rings for support
They contain smooth muscle but no cartilage
questions.explain: Bronchioles are about 0.5 mm wide, with smooth muscle for bronchodilation and bronchoconstriction but no cartilage.

questions.q: Parasympathetic (vagal) stimulation of the bronchial smooth muscle causes:
questions.explain: The vagus causes bronchoconstriction and gland secretion. Sympathetic beta 2 stimulation causes bronchodilation.

questions.q: Which pontine center adjusts the rate and pattern of breathing, modifying the pace set by the medulla?
options: Dorsal horn of the spinal cord
questions.explain: The respiratory rhythmicity center (medulla) sets the pace and initiates breathing; the apneustic center (pons) adjusts intensity (depth); the pneumotaxic center (pons) adjusts rate and pattern.

questions.q: A mother in premature labor is treated with cortisol-type therapy. What is the aim?
questions.explain: Cortisol is crucial for lung development, so it is given when preterm delivery is expected.
